No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. </details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ee2cd6e78bbe061d844f8b50ffd9d324d0fb27bb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/25297-mcp-standalone-actions-merged-listing.md, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-package-object-discovery.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/mcp-resume-run.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/index.ts, packages/runtime/package.json, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts, packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts, content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, AGENTS.md

Inputs read: card #25297 (body, comments 6351973228 and the claim 6352041231), PR #25304 (body, file list, comments 6352627434 and the `dogfood_battery` record 6352879348), the net diff `fb7501bc66..ee2cd6e78b` (merge base confirmed as `fb7501bc66`, 5 files, +426/-19), the cited code at the head, and the head's 41 check-runs, read last.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The published declaration surface of `@objectstack/runtime` does not move — right.** `packages/runtime/package.json` publishes one `exports` entry, `.`, onto `dist/index.*`; `src/index.ts` exports none of `collectActionDeclarations`, `resolveActionByName`, `invokeBusinessAction`, `resumeActionRun`, `buildMcpBridge` or `readMergedItems`, and re-exports nothing from `./action-execution.js` or `./domains/mcp.js` (its `HttpDispatcher`, `AppPlugin` and `collectBundleActions` exports are untouched by the diff). Each of the four changed functions gains one optional trailing input (`actions`, or the `readActions` wiring member); `readMergedItems` is module-private and only its type union widens by `'action'`; `McpMergedMetadataRead` is unchanged; the bridge's `listActions`, `runAction` and `resumeRun` signatures are unchanged. No accept set an author writes against moves: the diff touches no `packages/spec` file and no Zod schema.

2. **The merged action listing is read through the one existing unwrap, not a second copy of the merge — right.** `readServedActions` is `readMergedItems(await getProtocol(), 'action')`, the same function the skill read and `readMergedObjects` go through; the diff adds no second parse of `getMetaItems`'s answer, and the three outcomes are the documented ones: `undefined` on structural absence (no protocol in the slot or no `getMetaItems` verb) falls back to `loadMany('action')`, a throw travels to the caller, and a non-array answer without `items` reads as an empty listing, exactly as for `object`.

3. **Each numbered item of the PR body's Contract list reads right against the code.**
   - Item 1 (`list_actions`, a `manifest`-registered package's object-less action or an environment-authored one). Old: `MetadataManager.loadMany` iterates `this.loaders` alone (metadata-manager.ts), so neither the registry's item nor a `sys_metadata` row was in shape 2. New: the merged listing is the registry's `listItems('action')`, the environment's overlay rows and `metadataService.list('action')` merged by `readFlattenedMetaItems`, and the listing still passes through `isSystemObjectName`, `isHeadlessInvokableAction`, the handler probe, `actionAiExposureError` and `actionPermissionError` in `listActions`. Right.
   - Item 2 (`run_action`). Old: the two messages `Action 'NAME' not found` and `Action 'NAME' not found on object 'OBJECT'` are `invokeBusinessAction`'s own on a `null` resolution. New: resolved from the same collection, then the exposure, permission, activation (`disabledActionRefusal`), declared-param, confirmation and subject-record gates run unchanged. Right.
   - Item 3 (`resume_run`). Old: an empty candidate set throws `firstRefusal ?? resumeDoorError(..., 403)`; new: the standalone flow action is a candidate and `resumeAdmissionRefusal` admits it. Pinned on doubles, as the item says. Right.
   - Item 4 (a package's top-level action bound to one of its objects). The registry's `action` map holds bound top-level actions (`boundCodeActions` in registry.ts reads them), and the merged object listing folds the same action into the object's `actions[]` (#25139); `collectActionDeclarations` keys shape 1 first into `seen` as `objectName:name` and the standalone loop `continue`s on a seen key, so the object-embedded copy wins and the answer does not change. Right.
   - Item 5 (the narrowing: a disabled compiled-artifact package's object-less action). The artifact door registers every `packages[]` body's items with that body's own id (`registerArtifactBodyCollections` with `artifactPackageId(body)`, plugin.ts, ADR-0130 D4) into both its `MemoryLoader` and the manager, so `loadMany('action')` keeps the copy after a disable while the merged listing re-applies `isItemOfDisabledPackage` on its final set for every type but `package` (protocol.ts). So it is omitted from `list_actions`, `run_action` answers the two not-found spellings, and `resume_run` refuses 403 from the empty candidate set, as item 5 says ("derived, not pinned" for the last). Right.
   - Item 6 (the merged `action` listing throws). `readMergedItems` lets the throw travel; `listActions` awaits `readServedActions()` before calling `collectActionDeclarations`, and the two wirings await `readActions?.()` the same way, so the protocol's error reaches the caller and `loadMany` is never asked; old behaviour was the `try`/`catch` answering none. Right.

4. **The narrowing is stated wherever it should be — right.** PR title `fix(runtime)!:` and body `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; Contract item 5 named as the narrowing; changeset summary with `!` and "a disabled package's is omitted", its `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line, its BREAKING banner naming exactly that narrowing, the "Also changed" bullet and the "What to do" bullet; the test file's docblock names the last table row as the narrowing; `collectActionDeclarations`'s docblock ("an artifact package's action outlived the package's disable there") and `readServedActions`'s docblock ("a disabled artifact package's still was") carry it in the code. One wording note, not a defect: the changeset's "Also changed" bullet spells only the unscoped `Action 'NAME' not found`; the scoped spelling is in the PR body.

5. **The "Unchanged" claims hold — right.** Object-embedded actions: shape 1 of `collectActionDeclarations` is untouched. Object-embedded wins on a clash: the `seen` logic is untouched. REST's `/actions` door: `resolveRouteActionDeclaration` still resolves through `ql.getSchema` or `registry.getObject`, `registry.getItem('action', name)` and `loadDiagnosed`, and `domains/actions.ts` is not in the diff. The activation-ambiguity caller: `refuseAmbiguousActionActivation` calls `collectActionDeclarations(deps, meta)` with neither input, so it reads `listObjects()` and `loadMany('action')` as before. A host with no `protocol` service: `getProtocol()` answers `undefined`, `readMergedItems` answers `undefined`, `readServedActions` answers `undefined`, `actions` is falsy and the `loadMany` branch with its `try`/`catch` runs as before. The compiled artifact's actions: the merged listing lays the registry and overlay rows over `metadataService.list(type)`, which merges the loaders with the `register()` registry, so the artifact door's copy is served where its package is enabled; pinned as the control on both shapes.

6. **Reading the served face (`getMetaItems`) for a declaration `run_action` executes is sound against `getMetaItemsForExecution`'s documented rule — right.** Both faces are `readFlattenedMetaItems`; `audience` decides only whether `decorateMetadataItems` (a per-item `_diagnostics` member) and per-type redaction are applied, plus the served-only `flowRegistrationsOf` on the response envelope, so the item set is identical by construction ("every source, merge and filter above that line is shared"). `BUILTIN_METADATA_TYPE_REDACTORS` holds `datasource` alone, so an `action` body is served unredacted, and the fields the gates and dispatch read (`name`, `objectName`/`object`, `type`, `target`, `ai`, `requiredPermissions`, the declared params, `_packageId`) are the stored ones. The execution face's docblock says never to call it from a door that answers a caller, HTTP and MCP named, so the served face is the documented read for this door. Residual, not a defect: a redactor registered at runtime for `action` through `registerMetadataTypeRedactor` would redact every door's copy including this one; none exists in-tree.

7. **Each tool now makes two merged reads per call (object and action), and on an unscoped kernel each merged read hydrates overlay rows into the registry** — a pre-existing class of side effect since the #25120 object read and the skill read, not a new one. Noted, not a finding.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/runtime': patch` matches what the diff publishes. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no spec key, authorable spelling, metadata type, default or stored shape moves. Under the Post-Task rule in AGENTS.md ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition") the changeset keeps the `**BREAKING**` banner and exactly one disposition marker, the adr-0087 comment marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, in the shape the gate's header documents. The marker's own category reasoning matches the code: the package publishes, no ADR-0087 id is named, and nothing exported is removed or narrowed. `no-migration-prescription` is honest statement-against-statement: the body prescribes nothing to rewrite ("What to do. Nothing."), and the one consumer-visible change is a read the bridge no longer answers. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body, the spelling `readClause2Line` reads as declared with the `narrowing` arm; `breakingDeclaration` reads three signals on this changeset (the banner, the `!` summary, the arm) and the disposition it then asks for is present. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (the job carrying `check:adr-0087-registration` and the changeset level gate) are `success` on the head. The `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line is right: nothing an author writes widens, and the one accept-set change is the served read a disabled package's object-less action no longer gets.

### ③ Boundary flags

PR body's Acceptance notes:

- **The card's environment-authored control was not green at the base — judged right from the code.** `loadMany` walks the registered loaders only. `MetadataManager` wires a `DatabaseLoader` only from its constructor when `config.datasource && config.driver` are both given (`setDatabaseDriver`'s one in-tree caller), `setDataEngine` has no in-tree caller outside tests, and both skip on an `environmentId`. The rig's `MetadataPlugin` passes neither option on either shape, so no loader reads `sys_metadata` and the `saveMetaItem` row was invisible to `loadMany` on both shapes. The card's ask is met in the direction the code allows: the pins carry the compiled artifact's object-less action as the green-at-base control and the authored action as a red-at-base pin, on both shapes and both registrations; the correction is written on the card (claim 6352041231) and in the PR. Answered.
- **The narrowing is the artifact loader's copy — right** (①.3 item 5); a `manifest`-registered package's action lives in the registry alone, whose `listItems` already drops a disabled package's items.
- **REST's door still runs a disabled package's object-less action — escalated.** #25296 is open, dispatched, and carries PR #25305; `domains/actions.ts` is not in this diff. The resulting divergence (MCP omits, REST runs, on a disabled package only) is the card's own ask ("omitted, as its objects are"). Answered by escalation.
- **The served listing, not the execution one — answered** (①.6).
- **Two merged reads per call — a cost note**, answered in ①.7; no gate reads it.
- **`refuseAmbiguousActionActivation` still collects from `loadMany('action')` — right**, and #25296's card already carries the ask to measure whether that caller must move; it is not this card's.
- **Branch name `claude/project-thread-dkk3hd`** — the card's newest `Claim:` names that branch and the check-run "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" is `success`; the Duplicate Fix Guard concern is advisory.

Card's own asks:

- **Standalone actions from the merged view REST resolves from, not a second copy — met.** Nothing is copied into the metadata service; the bridge reads `getMetaItems({ type: 'action' })`, the read `GET /api/v1/meta/action` serves, through the one unwrap. Read precisely: REST's `/actions` door resolves one name through the registry (`registry.getItem`) and `loadDiagnosed` rather than through `getMetaItems`; the protocol's merged listing is the one merged view over that same registry and the overlay, and the one input the two doors now answer differently is a disabled package's action, which is the card's ask and #25296's door.
- **Object-embedded wins kept — met** (①.3 item 4, ①.5).
- **Every downstream MCP gate kept — met**: `ai.exposed`, `requiredPermissions`, the activation switch, headless-invokability, the handler probe, the declared params, `ai.requiresConfirmation`, the subject-record load under RLS and the `sys_` fail-close all sit after collection and are untouched by the diff.
- **A disabled package's global action omitted — met** (the compiled artifact's through the merged listing's filter, pinned on both shapes; a `manifest`-registered one through `listItems`, pinned on both shapes).
- **Pins on both kernel shapes with an environment-authored control — met**, with the correction judged above; 38 real-kernel cases in the #25120 rig and 3 unit cases.

Gates on the head: all 41 check-runs are `completed`; the five required contexts (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`) and all six `Test Core` shards are `success`; `Check Changeset` is `success`; the `skipped` runs are the jobs that skip on pull requests by design (the three `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards, `Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Build Docs`, two opt-in harnesses). The full dogfood battery the `!` and the `(narrowing)` arm owe was run on this head and posted as the `dogfood_battery` record 6352879348: Test Files 289 passed / 3 skipped, Tests 2491 passed / 18 skipped, 0 failed. No gate-carrying run is in progress or unsuccessful.

Residuals for the implementer, none of them a FAIL: `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx` still describes the listing as a walk of "every registered object's `actions[]`" and never names object-less actions or the `global` object key, before and after this PR; a docs-only follow-up could say so. The ablation legs are the PR's own report; this review is read-only and takes the head's check-runs as the gate verdicts.
